title: Robot Material Customization Workshop
description: A robot stands on a coffee mat serving as a workshop platform. The user acts as a materials engineer, applying and tweaking various PBR material properties across different body parts of the robot — adjusting metalness, roughness, emissive glow, color, and opacity — then validating the final configuration meets target specifications.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads both robot.glb and coffeemat.glb using GLTFLoader. Place the coffeemat flat on the ground as a workshop platform (scale it up ~3x). Position the robot standing centered on top of the coffeemat. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 2, 4) looking at the robot, with OrbitControls for rotation/zoom. Add an ambient light (intensity 0.4), a directional light from upper-right (intensity 1.2) with shadows enabled, and a subtle hemisphere light for fill. Implement raycasting so clicking on any robot mesh part selects it, highlighting it with a colored outline or emissive pulse. Create an HTML overlay panel (styled, semi-transparent dark background) on the right side with these material controls for the selected part: (1) Base Color picker (hex input), (2) Metalness slider 0-1 with 0.01 step, (3) Roughness slider 0-1 with 0.01 step, (4) Emissive color picker and emissive intensity slider 0-3, (5) Opacity slider 0-1 with transparent toggle checkbox. Each slider must show its current numeric value. Add a 'Validate Configuration' button that checks these target specs: at least 2 different robot parts must have metalness > 0.8, at least 1 part must have roughness < 0.2, at least 1 part must have emissive intensity > 1.0, and the coffeemat must have its color changed from default. Display validation results as a checklist with green checkmarks or red crosses. Also add a 'Reset All Materials' button that restores original materials. Make the coffeemat also selectable and editable. The coffeemat should have a subtle environment reflection. Use an environment map via RGBELoader or a simple CubeCamera for reflections. Ensure all materials are MeshStandardMaterial or MeshPhysicalMaterial. The scene background should be a dark gradient or neutral color (#1a1a2e). Add a step counter in the top-left showing how many material modifications have been made.
